title.en: Two approaches can belong to the same person
title.zh: 同一个人可以使用两种方式

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创情境：两位虚构读者准备参加一次低风险手工活动。一人想先做一个练习，另一人想先问清材料能否替换；他们可以先问一个关键问题，再各自决定是否尝试。不愿参加也可以。这里可讨论的是试做能回答什么、还缺什么条件，而不是给行动与谨慎排高低。
paragraphs.en: An additional original scene: Two fictional readers consider a low-risk craft activity. One wants to try an exercise; the other wants to ask whether materials can be substituted. They can ask one key question before each decides whether to try, and either can decline the activity. Discuss what a trial could answer and which conditions remain unknown, without ranking action above caution or caution above action.

title.en: One optional review of a real task

paragraphs.zh: 可选讨论提示：“这件事先核对哪一条条件就足够开始，哪些问题需要实际试过才知道？”可以只针对上面的虚构情境，分别说清可选做法、现实限制和仍然未知的信息。参与者可以不同意、暂不决定或结束讨论；无需用次数证明身份，也不要求他人改变做法。
paragraphs.en: An optional discussion prompt asks: “Which condition needs checking before starting, and which questions would require a trial?” Use only the fictional situation to distinguish possible approaches, practical constraints and information still unknown. Participants may disagree, leave a decision open or stop. Counts need not prove an identity or require anyone to change their approach.

paragraphs.zh: 补充场景与讨论提示由费马测试编辑部原创，可以只讨论虚构人物，也可以略过；不要求披露真实经历、展示答卷或照做。题目问当前更自然的相对选择，没有固定回顾天数。二十四题按连续四组六题记录，每题A或B只给该选项标明的一侧加一次；A／B对应侧逐题交替，每组各有三题A对应第一侧，因此全选A或全选B均为四组3:3，并不是固定选同一端。二十四次选择全部有效才显示任何个人记录；没有跳过或不计分选项，不适合时可以退出读公开指南，不以零、中点或别组补答。每组两侧各0—6次且合计六次，3:3保留两侧；6:0中的零只表示本组六个选项未选该侧，不是现实中不会使用它。相同次数可来自不同题目，不说明相同经历、实际频率、特质强度或人群百分位。两侧在现实中可以先后使用，四组分开计数不证明统计独立，也不拼成总分、人格、心理年龄、成熟等级或能力结论。UCSF应对研究资料和其他量表只提供概念背景，不能验证这套原创题本或英文工作译文；信效度、常模、语言等价和变化阈值尚未确立。页面仅在当前内存保留回答与记录，不保存草稿或结果缓存，刷新、换语、离开及历史恢复按现有流程清除。复制只包含四份公开指南标题与链接，不含次数、选项或作答标识；不同参与者不必交换记录，也不需要选出更好的应对者。
paragraphs.en: FermatMind Editorial authored the additional scenes and prompts. Discuss fictional people only or decline; no real history, answers or prescribed action is required. Questions ask which approach feels more natural at present, with no fixed recall period. Four consecutive six-choice groups count each A or B once for the side named by that option. A/B side assignments alternate by item, with A naming the first side in three items per group. All A or all B therefore gives four 3:3 ties rather than choosing the same side throughout. All 24 choices must be valid before any personal record appears. There is no skip or unscored option; leave and read public guides if neither fits, without zero, midpoint or cross-group substitution. Each side counts 0–6 selections and the pair sums to six. At 3:3 both sides remain; zero in 6:0 means no selection for that side in these six alternatives, not its absence from everyday life. Equal counts can come from different items and establish no equal experiences, real-life frequency, trait strength or percentile. Both approaches can occur in sequence. Separate counting establishes no statistical independence, overall score, personality, psychological age, maturity grade or ability conclusion. UCSF coping resources and other measures offer conceptual background without validating this original form or its working English translation. Reliability, validity, norms, language equivalence and meaningful-change thresholds remain unestablished. Responses and records stay in current-page memory without drafts or result caches; reloading, changing language, leaving and history restoration follow the existing clearing flow. Copying includes only four public guide titles and links, with no counts, options or attempt identifiers. Participants need not exchange records or select a better coper.

title.en: Both can happen in one sequence
title.zh: 两种做法可以先后发生

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创情境：虚构读者收到一则好消息，想先独自体会，再问朋友是否有空听一小段。朋友暂时没空，双方可以另约，也可以不分享细节。先独处、后表达不与任何一侧次数冲突；倾听者有无余力和表达者想透露多少，都需要当下确认，记录不能代替这些约定。
paragraphs.en: An additional original scene: A fictional reader receives good news, takes it in alone and then asks whether a friend has time to hear a small part. The friend is unavailable, so they may arrange another time or leave the details private. Private reflection followed by expression is compatible with either count. Available listening capacity and desired disclosure need present agreement, which no record supplies.

paragraphs.zh: 可选讨论提示：“现在想先整理什么，若选择交流，怎样确认对方是否愿意听？”可以只针对上面的虚构情境，分别说清可选做法、现实限制和仍然未知的信息。参与者可以不同意、暂不决定或结束讨论；无需用次数证明身份，也不要求他人改变做法。
paragraphs.en: An optional discussion prompt asks: “What needs sorting out first, and if conversation is wanted, how could willingness to listen be checked?” Use only the fictional situation to distinguish possible approaches, practical constraints and information still unknown. Participants may disagree, leave a decision open or stop. Counts need not prove an identity or require anyone to change their approach.

title.en: Adjust the method while keeping an anchor
title.zh: 调整方法，也可以保留支点

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创情境：虚构小组原定在室外整理一批展板，天气变化后转到室内。他们可以改工作顺序，同时保留一项必要的材料检查，并说明谁负责确认。改变路径与保留检查点可以并存；是否完成、检查是否足够，仍需看实际过程，不由六次选择判断。
paragraphs.en: An additional original scene: A fictional group plans to organize display boards outside and moves indoors when the weather changes. They can change the work order while keeping a necessary materials check and naming who will confirm it. A changed route can coexist with a retained checkpoint. Completion and adequate checking still depend on the actual process, rather than six selections.

title.en: One optional review of a changed plan

paragraphs.zh: 可选讨论提示：“这次哪些步骤能调整，哪个检查点仍有现实理由保留，谁需要知道？”可以只针对上面的虚构情境，分别说清可选做法、现实限制和仍然未知的信息。参与者可以不同意、暂不决定或结束讨论；无需用次数证明身份，也不要求他人改变做法。
paragraphs.en: An optional discussion prompt asks: “Which steps can change, which checkpoint still has a practical reason to remain, and who needs to know?” Use only the fictional situation to distinguish possible approaches, practical constraints and information still unknown. Participants may disagree, leave a decision open or stop. Counts need not prove an identity or require anyone to change their approach.

title.en: A day and a longer plan can support each other
title.zh: 当天安排与长期计划可以并存

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创情境：虚构读者原想用空闲晚上预习下月课程，但当天需要休息。他可以先休息、改约预习时间，也可以暂不作新安排；是否还有未来任务，应另行确认。这个例子不指定哪种生活更好，也不把能提前准备的资源差异读成成熟差异。
paragraphs.en: An additional original scene: A fictional reader intended to use a free evening to prepare for next month’s course but needs rest today. Resting first, moving preparation or leaving a new arrangement undecided are possible. Any remaining future task needs its own check. This example prescribes no better way of life and treats available preparation resources as no maturity ranking.

title.en: One optional comparison of two needs

paragraphs.zh: 可选讨论提示：“今天真正需要回应什么，之后的约定有哪些，当前时间能支持到哪里？”可以只针对上面的虚构情境，分别说清可选做法、现实限制和仍然未知的信息。参与者可以不同意、暂不决定或结束讨论；无需用次数证明身份，也不要求他人改变做法。
paragraphs.en: An optional discussion prompt asks: “What needs attention today, which later commitments exist, and what does the available time allow?” Use only the fictional situation to distinguish possible approaches, practical constraints and information still unknown. Participants may disagree, leave a decision open or stop. Counts need not prove an identity or require anyone to change their approach.
